name: Lactin-V
question: Does intravaginal Lactin-V after treatment of acute cystitis prevent recurrent urinary tract infection in premenopausal women?

design.population: Premenopausal women aged 18–40 years with treated acute uncomplicated cystitis and at least one prior treated symptomatic UTI in the preceding 12 months.
design.description: Single-center, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 2 randomized trial
design.locator: Methods, Participants, Randomization and Study Design; Results, Enrollment and Demographics

verdictNote: Vaginal colonization increased; the recurrent-UTI confidence interval crossed the null.
takeaway: Intravaginal Lactobacillus crispatus CTV-05 (Lactin-V) after cystitis treatment yielded fewer recurrent UTIs than placebo over 10 weeks, but the confidence interval included no reduction; high-level vaginal L. crispatus colonization was more frequent with Lactin-V.

reports.label: Phase 2 primary report
reports.citation: Stapleton AE, Au-Yeung M, Hooton TM, et al. "Randomized, Placebo-Controlled Phase 2 Trial of a Lactobacillus crispatus Probiotic Given Intravaginally for Prevention of Recurrent Urinary Tract Infection." *Clin Infect Dis.* 2011;52(10):1212-1217. doi:10.1093/cid/cir183
reports.followUp: Scheduled visits at 1 and 10 weeks after starting suppositories

results.measure: At least one symptomatic, pyuria-positive, culture-confirmed UTI by 10 weeks
results.note: Two randomized participants per arm were not in the recurrence analysis. The published report gives no prespecified alpha; the confidence interval includes 1. UTI required symptoms, pyuria (at least 8 WBC/high-power field), and positive urine culture.
results.locator: Results, Clinical Outcomes; Table 2; Methods, Participants

results.measure: At 10-week visit, at least 10^6 16S rRNA gene copies per vaginal swab
results.note: The report identifies colonization as part of its primary objective and calls the comparison significant; it does not specify a formal alpha threshold.
results.locator: Methods, Sample Size, Objectives; Results, Clinical Outcomes

harms.label: Any reported adverse effect
harms.locator: Results, Safety and Tolerability; Results, Enrollment and Demographics
harms.note: Most common reported effects were vaginal discharge, itching, or moderate abdominal discomfort; per-symptom arm counts were not given.

harms.label: Treatment discontinuation for adverse effects
harms.locator: Results, Safety and Tolerability; Results, Enrollment and Demographics
harms.note: The single discontinuation was in the placebo arm.

harms.label: Bacterial vaginosis or candidal vaginitis
harms.note: The paper reports the 0–5% range for these conditions across both arms, without condition-specific arm counts.

harms.label: Pyelonephritis
harms.locator: Results, Safety and Tolerability; Results, Enrollment and Demographics
harms.note: No episodes were reported in either group.

delivery.label: Suppository regimen
delivery.value: After standard treatment for acute cystitis, self-administered gelatin vaginal capsule without applicator (Lactin-V 10^8 CFU/mL or placebo), daily for 5 days, then weekly for 10 weeks.
